stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Row6: 8 8 8 (cols4-6), row7: 8 3 8 8 8 (cols4-8), row8: 8 9 8 8 (cols4-7)... Actually shape:
```
8 8 8
8 3 8 8 8
8 9 8 8
```
Hmm there's a 9 inside at (8,5) — the "hole". The motif: an 8-outline of an L/diamond plus 9? Let me decode: cells 8 form shape; 9 inside. This looks like the template: 2x3 block of 8s with 9 at position... And lone 3 gets this motif stamped.

Output added cells around 3@(9,17): rows8-10 cols16-20:
row8: 8 8 8 (16,17,18), row9: 8 3 8 8 8 (16..20), row10: 8 9 8 8 (16,18,19,20?) let me check output rows 8-12 cols16-21:
row8: ... 8 8 8 at 16,17,18
row9: 8 3 8 8 8 at 16-20
row10: 8 9 8 8 at 16,17,18? output row10: cols: positions ... "9 9 8 9 8 8 9" hmm.

The stamped motif copies the input motif exactly. So rule: each isolated cell of color X gets a stamp = the template associated with it, placed relative to the marker matching where marker sits in the template. In demo3: template has 3 at (7,5); stamp anchors so 3 lands at same relative position. Isolated 3@(9,17) got full motif stamped. What about the other isolated 2@(13,23)? Nothing added! Hmm — maybe only some colors get stamps, or the 2/7 pair forms its own motif (2 above, 7 below) and already complete.

So rule: for each color that appears BOTH as part of a multi-cell motif and isolated, stamp the motif anchored on the marker. Test input: isolated 2s and 3s; motifs present: 9-column (rows16-17 col1-2 vertical 2x1 of 9s) with 2@(17,2) adjacent — incomplete motif of 9s+2? And 6-cluster rows20-22: 6@(20,9),6@(21,7),(21,8),6@(22,9),3@(21,9). So 6-motif contains 3@(21,9). Isolated 3s would get the 6-motif stamped (anchor the 3 at its position within the motif). Isolated 2s would get the 9-motif? The 9-motif: 9@(16,1),9@(17,1),2@(17,2). Anchor 2 at (17,2) position: offsets of 9s relative to 2: (-1,-1),(0,-1). Stamp those.

But demo1/demo2 don't show stamps for 2s... Demo1 stamp for isolated 2 was four 4s; isolated 3 one 7. Those could be parts of larger motifs too: 4@(20,12)... pre-existing 4-motif rows20-22 cols11-12:
```
. 4 .
2 4 .
4 4 .
```
i.e., 2@(21,11) with 4s at offsets (-1,+1),(0,+1),(+1,0),(+1,+1). Isolated 2@(4,5) got 4s at offsets (-1,-1),(0,-1),(+1,-1),(+1,0). Different — mirror horizontally. And isolated 2@(16,11) got offsets (-1,-1),(0,-1),(+1,-1),(+1,0) same. Hmm both consistent. But why mirror vs original? Maybe because direction must avoid overlapping existing structure / or chosen consistently by e.g. pointing left always? The test grid has 2s... need the actual stamp shapes from templates in test itself: 9-motif anchor 2 at (17,2): 9s at (-1,-1),(0,-1) relative to 2. 6-motif: 3@(21,9) with 6s at offsets (-1,0)= (20,9), (0,-2)=(21,7), (0,-1)=(21,8), (+1,0)=(22,9). Hmm irregular.

But wait — maybe the rule isn't mirroring; maybe direction depends on something. In demo1, pre-existing 4-motif has 2@(21,11) with 4s to the right/below-right. Isolated 2 got 4s to the LEFT/same-ish. If the rule were "stamp a copy of the template", then isolated 2 should get the EXACT same offsets (right side). Unless the rule is that the motif orientation points away from nearest edge or existing stuff... For demo1, both stamps used left offsets, whereas template used right. That means the template orientation flips per instance — perhaps determined by which side has more space? Both free though. Or maybe the stamp attaches mirrored such that... Alternatively maybe the real rule: the marker indicates where a shape goes and the shape's orientation determined by the marker's relation to nearest other marker of another color? 2@(4,5) has 3@(10,5) below → shape extends up-left? eh.

Alternatively, simpler: the stamp for a 2 is {( -1,−1),(0,−1),(+1,−1),(+1,0)} (left-bowed), and the pre-existing motif at rows20-22 is just the INPUT showing what the stamp looks like but with its 2 at bottom-middle. And demo1's 2 stamps match that. Check the 3 stamp: 3@(10,5)->7@(11,5); pre-existing 3/7 motif: 3@(10,13),7@(11,13): 7 offset (+1,0) ✓. Consistent! Great: 3→single cell below as 7.

And demo2: 3s stamp 6s at offsets (0,+1),(+1,0) — but demo1 said 3→below-only?? Contradiction between demos?! Demo1 3@ (10,5): only 7 below; demo2 3@ (0,4): 6 right + 6 below.

Unless demo2's 3s have different partners... demo2 isolated 3 stamps 6s at right and down. Demo1 isolated 3 stamps 7 below only. These can't be the same rule... unless in demo2 the marker is 3 but partner color is 6, and the shape differs. Hmm, wait — maybe the stamp shape differs based on the PARTNER COLOR's template: i.e., stamp = template of the OTHER color. In demo1, partner of 2 is 4: the 4-template... The 2s' stamps are made of 4s with shape S1={( -1,−1),(0,−1),(+1,−1),(+1,0)}. The 3s' stamps are 7s single cell below. In demo2, 3s get 6s: two cells. In demo3, 3s get 8-shape with 9.

So the stamp shape is per-color-pair and differs per demo?! That's impossible unless shape derives from context. UNLESS: the stamp = the full multi-cell motif containing that color elsewhere in the grid, oriented toward the nearest other instance of either color.

Demo1: 2@(4,5) — nearest same/paired structure is the 4-motif below-right (the pre-existing 4-cluster). Its orientation: 2@(21,11) with 4s at rel {(-1,+1),(0,+1),(+1,0),(+1,+1)}. Stamped shape {(-1,-1),(0,-1),(+1,-1),(+1,0)}. Mirror horizontal. Hmm if the shape were rotated/reflected depending on direction... 

Actually, wait — maybe I misread and the correct interpretation: the stamp orientation is determined by pointing away from the template location. In demo1, 2@(4,5): the 4-motif is BELOW-RIGHT of it. The stamp placed 4s to the LEFT. Weird.

Alternative: the stamp mirrors because the shape is meant to "point at" the other color instance? Like the motif rotates so the marker faces the nearest other marker? Meh.

Let me instead consider demo3: 2@(13,23) got NOTHING. Why? Because its pair-partner 7 is already... no 7 near. Hmm. But maybe rule: stamp only colors that exist as markers AND have a template; 2 has no template (the 2 in 9-motif... it does!). Hmm 2@(13,23) didn't get anything. So maybe rule applies only to certain colors. In demo3, 3 got stamped, 2 not. In demo2, 3 got stamped. Demo1: 2 got stamped, 3 got stamped. Hmm inconsistent again... unless the trigger color relates to background: demo1 bg=8? no bg was 8. colors 2,3,4,7. Demo2 bg=0, colors 3,6. Demo3 bg=9, colors 2,3,8,9? 9 is background. So non-bg: 8(motif),3,2. Stamp happened for 3, not 2.

Maybe rule: stamp happens for the color whose instances in the motif... hmm. In demo1, stamped colors: 2 and 3 (both). Demo3: only 3 stamped; 2 not. Difference: in demo3, is there a completed motif for 2? The 2@(13,23) has NO 8s nearby — nothing to suggest how to stamp. In demo1, 2@(4,5) has no template either... but it did get stamped. Ugh.

Hmm wait, maybe demo1's stamps ARE templates defined by the motif containing 4s AND the fact that isolated 2s exist: the 4-motif defines the stamp for 2, and isolated 3s define stamp for 3 using the 3-7 motif (7 below). Demo3's motif: 3 inside 8-shape; isolated 3 gets 8-stamp; isolated 2 gets nothing because 2 isn't inside any motif — the motif contains 3 but not 2. Demo2's motif: 3 with 6s; isolated 3s get 6-stamp. And what stamps 2? None exist in demos. So rule: for each isolated cell of color X, stamp the full motif containing X, with the marker at its position in the motif.

Check demo1: motif containing 2: the 4-motif. Isolated 2 should get 4-stamp with 2@(21,11)'s offsets... but isolated 2s got the MIRRORED offsets {(-1,-1),(0,-1),(+1,-1),(+1,0)}. Mismatch unless orientation flip. Hmm. Unless I'm wrong that motif's 2 is at (21,11). Input demo1 row20: col12=4; row21: col11=2,col12=4; row22: col11=4,col12=4. Offsets of 4s relative to 2: (-1,+1),(0,+1),(+1,0),(+1,+1). Isolated 2 got (-1,-1),(0,-1),(+1,-1),(+1,0). Definitely mirrored horizontally. Weird.

Unless... the stamp is placed to point AWAY from the motif source? Or maybe the actual rule involves rotation based on position parity? Both isolated 2s in demo1 are to the left of their respective motifs? The stamp for 2@(4,5) placed 4s left; stamp for 2@(16,11) also left. The motif's 2 has 4s to its right. So when stamping a 2, the shape is mirrored — as if the stamp is attached on the opposite side of where the motif's 4s attach relative to its 2? No—the stamp's 2 gets 4s to its left, motif's 2 gets 4s to right. That's exactly reflection through vertical axis. Why?

Maybe the transformation includes a global horizontal flip for the stamp? Or maybe the rule: the stamp reflects across the line connecting markers? Overthinking. Alternative: maybe the stamp is placed so that it points TOWARD the motif? no.

Hmm, alternatively the rule might involve the other color in the pair: 2's stamp uses 4s positioned so the whole thing mimics the 3-7 motif's relationship? Like pairs of motifs interlock?

Let me look at demo2 again: motif: 3@(0,11) with 6s at (0,12),(1,11) i.e. offsets (0,+1),(+1,0). Isolated 3s got same offsets (0,+1),(+1,0). Good, exact copy, no mirroring. So why did demo1 mirror?

Check demo1 pre-motif 2@(21,11) offsets again: row20: cols11,12: "4 ." wait output/input comp listed (20,12),(21,11),(21,12),(22,11),(22,12). Row20: only col12=4. Row21: 2@11, 4@12. Row22: 4@11,4@12. Offsets rel 2@(21,11): (-1,+1),(0,+1),(+1,0),(+1,+1). Stamp rel 2@(4,5): (-1,-1),(0,-1),(+1,-1),(+1,0). Mirror yes.

And demo1 3-stamp: motif 3@(10,13),7@(11,13): offset (+1,0). Stamp: (+1,0). Same.

Demo2 3-stamp: motif 3@(0,11) w/ 6s offsets (0,+1),(+1,0); stamp identical. So demo1's 2-case is the odd mirror. Possibly my earlier reading of demo1's stamp is wrong? Isolated 2@(4,5) adds: (3,4),(4,4),(5,4),(5,5). Relative: (-1,-1),(0,-1),(+1,-1),(+1,0). Yes mirror.

Hmm — OR maybe the rule isn't stamping the motif as-is but stamping its MIRROR when... direction chosen so that the shape points away from the original motif? Stamp near top-left corner area... The isolated 2s in demo1 are ABOVE the motif; the stamp puts 4s LEFT. Eh.

Alternatively maybe there are TWO motifs per color pair in demo1: the 4-motif might come in two orientations and the isolated ones use whichever orientation fits without touching edges... Both fit equally.

Or maybe the stamp orientation is determined by where the marker sits within the motif SHAPE as a connected component including the partner: In demo1, maybe relevant components include pairing: the isolated 2 gets stamped with 4s such that the result mimics the other motif but rotated 180°? Rotate motif offsets by 180: {(1,-1),(0,-1),(-1,0),(-1,-1)} = {(-1,-1),(-1,0),(0,-1),(1,-1)}. Our stamp lacks (-1,0). Not that.

Reflection across horizontal axis: {(1,1),(0,1),(-1,1),(-1,0)}. No.

Reflection across diagonal? Transpose: {(-1,+1),(+1,0),(0,+1),(0,+1)} no.

OK so it's pure horizontal mirror. Whatever the why, maybe the rule is: stamp the mirror image because the motif acts like a "mirror"... or maybe the true rule: extend the marker into the shape of the nearest multi-cell motif, positioned on the side AWAY from the motif. For isolated 2@(16,11): mirror gives 4s left; original would put 4s right — also fine. Hmm.

Time is short. Cheaper: request one more demo (we have 5 left, 0 wrong besides). A new demo could clarify whether stamps are mirrored or context-dependent. But honestly, given uncertainty, requesting another demo is the right move.

Actually wait. Let me reconsider. Maybe the orientation depends on the marker's own color value parity or its role. Demo1: 2→mirror, 3→same. Demo2: 3→same. Demo3: 3→same. Hmm all 3s same orientation, demo1's 2 mirrored. Maybe orientation depends on marker's color: even markers mirrored?? Test then needs: 2-stamps mirrored... but test has no 4s or template for 2! Test stamps come from 9-motif and 6-motif contained in test itself. Orientation question doesn't arise since we'd stamp the motifs as extracted, likely as-is.

Test motifs:
- 9-motif: 9@(16,1) and 9@(17,1), 2@(17,2). Anchor 2 at (17,2): 9s at offsets (-1,-1),(0,-1). Isolated 2s get 9s at those offsets. But wait — do all isolated 2s get stamped? Demo1: both 2s stamped. Demo3: the 2 NOT stamped. Difference: demo3's motif contains 3, not 2. So stamping applies for colors appearing IN A MOTIF. Demo1: 2 appears in motif (at (21,11)) → stamp 2s; 3 appears in motif (3@(10,13),7@(11,13)) → stamp 3s. Demo2: 3 in motif → stamp. Test: 3 appears in 6-motif → stamp 3s; 2 appears in 9-motif → stamp 2s. And the pre-existing motifs themselves unchanged.

Stamp shapes for test (from motifs, exact orientation as drawn):
- 9-stamp (anchor 2@(17,2)): add 9@(r-1,c-1), 9@(r,c-1) for each isolated 2.
- 6-stamp (anchor 3@(21,9)): 6s at (r-1,c), (r,c-2),(r,c-1),(r+1,c) for each isolated 3.

Hmm wait, but should the 3-motif anchor be the 3 at (21,9)? In the 6-motif, 3 is at (21,9) with 6s at (20,9),(21,7),(21,8),(22,9). But careful: is the motif really centered on 3, or should the stamp anchor differently? Demo3 shows anchor at the 3 matching position in motif. OK.

But hold on — should isolated 2s in test also be checked against 9-motif: is the 9-motif really a motif? It's 2 cells of 9 + a 2 — sparse. In demo3 the motif was dense. Risky but plausible: rule = every color appearing in a cluster gets stamped everywhere else.

Also: should stamping skip when cells occupied? Presumably skip occupied cells.

Also check demo1: does 3 appear in motif? 3@(10,13) with 7@(11,13): yes → stamp 3s ✓. And demo2: 3 with 6s → stamp 3s ✓. Demo3: only 3 in motif → 2s unstamped ✓✓. Consistent across all three demos! 

Also verify demo1: 4s and 7s appear in motifs but aren't isolated in input → only isolated markers get stamped. Demo1 stamp of 2 got 4-colored cells (partner color 4, from motif cells except the 2). And 3 stamp got 7s. ✓

Now apply to test grid: isolate = no neighboring non-zero cells. From earlier scan:
Isolated 3s: (1,3),(7,11),(9,7),(12,3),(20,2). Isolated 2s: (1,6),(1,10),(4,0),(4,9),(6,5),(7,2),(10,0),(12,8),(12,11),(13,5),(16,5),(16,8),(16,11),(19,5),(20,11),(23,4).

Apply 9-stamp (add 9 at (-1,-1) and (0,-1)) to each isolated 2 — but only if target cells are background 0? All targets are 0 presumably. Wait but 2 at (4,0): (4,-1) out of bounds. Handle bounds. Similarly (10,0). Also 2@(1,6),(1,10) fine.

Apply 6-stamp to each isolated 3: 6 at offsets (-1,0),(0,-2),(0,-1),(+1,0).

Wait, also demo1's 3 stamp: motif had 7 at (+1,0) only — stamp added only (+1,0). Consistent. Demo2's 3 stamp: offsets (0,+1),(+1,0). ✓

Hmm, but actually demo1: 2-stamp came from motif containing 2 (the 4-motif). Test's 2-motif is the 9-motif. But wait, is the 9-motif "the motif"? 9 might be a background-like color? Background in test is 0. Fine.

One concern: in test, the 9 column (16,1),(17,1) with 2@(17,2): anchor 2@(17,2): offsets (-1,-1),(0,-1). So stamp 9s at (-1,-1),(0,-1) for isolated 2s.

For isolated 3s, stamp from 6-motif: 3@(21,9): 6s offsets (-1,0),(0,-2),(0,-1),(+1,0).

Hmm wait, check demo1's 2-mirror anomaly again — it doesn't matter for test since test's motifs are read directly.

Risk: maybe the demo1 mirror suggests orientation flips when stamping. In test, motifs only occur once each; ambiguity about flip remains. Given cost, I'll go with direct-copy stamps. But actually the mirror case may hint the general principle: maybe the stamp is reflected across the axis such that the shape points away from... In demo3, stamp identical orientation. So no. Proceed with direct copy.

Compute final grid and submit.

# isolate clusters
def comps(g,bg):
    Hh,Ww=len(g),len(g[0]); cells=[(r,c) for r in range(Hh) for c in range(Ww) if g[r][c]!=bg]
    seen=set(); res=[]

# Systematize: for each demo, list all markers (single-cell comps) and shapes (multi-cell comps),
# and for each marker the observed stamped cells (rel offsets from marker position/color-matching),
# then infer the choice rule.
def comps(g,bg):
    H=len(g);W=len(g[0]);seen=set();out=[]
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if g[i][j]!=bg and (i,j) not in seen:
                st=[(i,j)];cells=set()
                while st:
                    a,b=st.pop()
                    if (a,b) in cells or not(0<=a<H and 0<=b<W) or g[a][b]==bg: continue
                    cells.add((a,b))
                    for dx in(-1,0,1):
                        for dy in(-1,0,1):
                            st.append((a+dx,b+dy))
                seen|=cells;out.append(sorted(cells))
    return out
from collections import Counter as Cntr
G=load()
for k in range(1,9):
    inp,out=G[f'Demo pair {k} input'],G[f'Demo pair {k} output']
    H,W=len(inp),len(inp[0]); bg=Cntr(x for r in inp for x in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    Cs=comps(inp,bg)
    multi=[c for c in Cs if len(c)>1]; singles=[next(iter(c)) for c in Cs if len(c)==1]
    print('pair',k,'shapes:',[(sorted({p:(inp[p[0]][p[1]]) for p in c}.items()),min(p for p in c)) for c in multi])
    print('   singles:',[(m,inp[m[0]][m[1]]) for m in singles])
